Role Details Title: Grantmaker-in-Residence (Leader of the X fund or Grantmaker in Y area also possible options) Location: Hybrid: remote with four mandatory in-person weeks (London; New York; San Francisco; a cause-track conference in London, Oxford, or Mexico depending on cause area) Compensation: A living stipend of ~$125,000 for the year Duration: 12 months, full-time, February 2027 – January 2028 Focus areas: Farmed animal welfare, philanthropic infrastructure, global health, global aid policy Goal: To create the next generation of fieldshapers and active grantmakers How to apply: Fill out this form (by October 30th) Program The Elevate Philanthropy fieldshaper program is a one-year training program that turns generalist, high-agency professionals into active grantmakers and general managers of problems. The program aims to create a pathway into philanthropy and to develop the next generation of grantmakers, with an emphasis on active deployment and ecosystem thinking. Developed by the co-founder of Ambitious Impact’s Charity Entrepreneurship program, an incubator behind 50+ high-impact charities, the program will train grantmakers who grow and affect the broader field they operate in. Residents join one of three cause tracks (Animal Welfare, Global Health, or Philanthropic Infrastructure) and complete a six-week bootcamp before deploying capital into a specific sub-area within their chosen track (e.g. effective careers, or fish welfare in Asia). After this, five months of weekly structured sessions will run alongside live grantmaking. In the second half of the year, this tapers to weekly coaching as residents scale their deployment. The program includes four in-person weeks: kick-off in London; one each at conferences in San Francisco and New York, and one at a cause-relevant conference (the AVA Summit or EAG London). These give fieldshapers time to get to know one another and to meet other grantmakers, funders, and actors in their field. The year closes with a published piece of thought leadership, a one-year grant portfolio, and a demo-day-style event where residents present how they deployed their funding. Each pool is structured as a fund, with ongoing opportunities (though not guarantees) for top-ups and increased funding volume. What You Will Do The key goal is to deploy $1,000,000 in grant capital over the year impactfully. Deploy the majority of capital actively, e.g. creating opportunities or finding funding options that other grantmakers would miss. Build a pipeline of ~20 funding opportunities in your cause track, run due diligence scaled to grant size, and make the case for or against funding to a review process. Long-term, you will also consider assessing grant opportunities beyond single organizations; looking at fund managers and pooled vehicles, as well as actively co-building new projects in the field. Complex judgment: For example, being able to weigh factors like the talent counterfactuals of a grant, and how a given project connects to the broader ecosystem. Coordination: For example, if it makes sense to build up a donor collaboration in your area, and if so, which actors would be best positioned to join it. The reason we are running this program is that we believe there is a shortage of great grantmakers relative to funding and the hiring needs of growing foundations. What We Are Looking For Traits: Rigor and intellectual honesty under ambiguity; decision-making grounded in evidence. Clear decision-making grounded in evidence and logic. Recruitment Process The recruitment vetting is an intense process, but we aim to make each of the steps useful for the candidates in assessing their fit with grantmaking as a career path.
